card.name: Kete
card.era: Asante royal court tradition (17th-18th century roots)
card.profile: Kete is a dance-music form originating among the Asante and performed by the Akan of Ghana, originally confined to the palace of the Asantehene and subchiefs entitled to a palanquin (Cambridge University Press; Ejisu Besease). The term refers simultaneously to a set of instruments, the music, and the dance. Danced barefoot by trained dancers with the lapa cloth lowered beneath the chest, its slow, dignified movements use symbolic hand gestures reflecting moral values; the music is reputed to attract good spirits (Cambridge). Individual pieces include Adaban, Apente and others, performed at royal funerals, festivals and durbars.
card.insight: Per R.S. Rattray's early-20th-century notes, Kete was 'taken to war' and played at Adae ceremonies, funerals and formerly at executions; the full Kete ensemble was the prerogative of the Asantehene (academic analysis of Asante Kete drumming).
